title: Deposits
purpose: When a deposit is taken, how much, and what is refunded.
facts: Deposit of half the part price for special-order parts and ordered electrical parts over 300 USD.
Transmission rebuild: 1,700.00, half of the specialist's price (catalogue transmission_rebuild sublet price 3,400.00).
Four or more tyres in a non-stocked size: half the tyre price. Company accounts: none.
Entered as a payment marked deposit (ERP payment: deposit).
Refund in full before shipping; after shipping less the supplier's restocking charge of up to 20 %; non-returnable parts become the customer's.
Refunds return by the original method; cash refunds need the shop manager.

rows.When: A special-order part, or any electrical part once ordered, that costs the customer more than $300
rows.Deposit: Half the price of the part

rows.When: A transmission going out for rebuild
rows.Deposit: $1,700.00, which is half of the specialist's price

rows.When: Four or more tires in a size we do not normally stock
rows.Deposit: Half the price of the tires
None. It goes on the statement

list_items.item: The customer cancels before the part has shipped: the whole deposit back.

After it has shipped: the deposit less whatever the supplier charges us to take it back, which can be up to 20 % of the part's price. If the supplier will not take it back, the part is the customer's and the deposit is kept.
A refund goes back the way the deposit came: card to card, cash to cash. A cash refund needs the shop manager: see Voids and refunds.

new_facts: Deposit amounts and the 20 % restocking ceiling. Reason: a deposit policy was asked for; the ERP's deposit payments must follow these rules (half, 1,700 for a rebuild).
